courses.scope_note: A short sample of reasoning and prerequisite knowledge. Practical performance and durable mastery need later practice.

questions.label: Resolve a relative path
questions.prompt: Your working directory is `/home/lee/project`. Where does `../notes` point?
questions.explanation: .. selects the parent directory before notes is resolved.

questions.label: Preserve filename boundaries
questions.prompt: In Bash, `file="quarter one.txt"`. Which command passes that filename as one argument?
questions.explanation: Double quotes preserve the expanded value as one argument; single quotes pass the literal dollar sign and name.

questions.label: Understand pipeline failure
questions.prompt: In Bash with pipefail disabled, what is the status of `false | true`?
questions.explanation: Without pipefail, the pipeline status is the status of its final command.

questions.label: Interpret file permissions
questions.prompt: A regular file has mode `640`. What can a member of its group do through those permission bits?
questions.explanation: The group digit 4 grants read, with no write or execute bit.

questions.label: Choose a cooperative stop
questions.prompt: A process supports graceful shutdown on TERM. Which first action gives it that opportunity?
questions.explanation: SIGTERM permits a handler to clean up; SIGKILL cannot be handled.

questions.label: Explain child environments
questions.prompt: A Bash script executed as `./setup.sh` runs `export COLOR=blue`. What happens to COLOR in its parent shell?
questions.explanation: An executed child inherits an environment but does not replace its parent environment.

questions.label: Resolve a relative path
questions.prompt: From `/srv/app`, what does `cd ./logs/..` select if logs is an ordinary subdirectory?
questions.explanation: Entering logs and then its parent returns to app.

questions.label: Preserve filename boundaries
questions.prompt: `name="two words"`. Which expansion supplies exactly one argument containing the value?
questions.explanation: Double quotes preserve the argument boundary while permitting expansion.

courses.scope_note: A short sample of reasoning and prerequisite knowledge. Practical performance and durable mastery need later practice.

questions.label: Forward arguments without splitting
questions.prompt: A wrapper must pass all its arguments to `tool` unchanged. Which invocation preserves each original boundary?
questions.explanation: Quoted "$@" expands each positional argument as its own argument.

questions.label: Make failure explicit
questions.prompt: Which branch reports failure only when `build` returns a nonzero status?

choices.text: if build; then printf "%s\n" failed >&2; fi
if ! build; then printf "%s\n" failed >&2; fi

questions.explanation: The negated command status selects the branch only when build fails.

questions.label: Build a command as arguments
questions.prompt: `files=("one file" "two file")`. Which expansion passes two file arguments?
questions.explanation: Quoted array-at preserves one word per array element.

questions.label: Recognize strict-mode limits
questions.prompt: Does `set -e` guarantee that every nonzero command status terminates a Bash script?

choices.text: No; command context changes its behavior
Yes, including commands used as if conditions

questions.explanation: Conditional tests and other documented contexts are exceptions; critical failure paths need explicit handling.

questions.label: Avoid publishing partial output
questions.prompt: A script must replace a local report only after generation and validation succeed. Which approach meets that goal?

choices.text: Append results directly and delete the report if generation fails
Write a temporary file in the destination directory, validate it, then rename it over the report

questions.explanation: Keeping the old report until validation and a same-filesystem rename avoids exposing partially generated content; crash durability needs additional measures.

questions.label: Design repeatable automation
questions.prompt: An installation script may run twice. Which behavior best supports safe repetition?

choices.text: Delete all existing settings before each run
Detect or converge the desired state before making changes
Append the same config block on every run

questions.explanation: Converging desired state avoids accumulating duplicate changes across runs.

questions.label: Forward arguments without splitting
questions.prompt: A wrapper receives `"a b"` and `c`. What argument count does `tool "$@"` pass to tool?
questions.explanation: Quoted at forwards the two original positional parameters.

questions.label: Make failure explicit
questions.prompt: `if deploy; then echo done; else exit 1; fi`. If deploy fails, which path runs?

choices.text: The else branch exits with status 1

questions.explanation: if tests the command status; nonzero takes the else branch.

questions.label: Order synchronous code and promise reactions
questions.explanation: The current job runs to completion before the promise reaction job runs.

questions.label: Track a captured binding
questions.explanation: The closure reads the binding rather than a frozen copy of its initial value.

questions.label: Distinguish queues
questions.prompt: After a click handler finishes, which normally runs first: an already-queued promise reaction or a zero-delay timer callback?

choices.text: They execute concurrently on the same main thread

questions.explanation: The microtask checkpoint drains queued promise reactions before the next timer task.

questions.label: Reason about reachability
questions.prompt: A listener on a long-lived window captures a large object. Why can that object remain in memory?

choices.text: The reachable listener retains a path to the captured object
Objects captured by functions are always leaked permanently
Garbage collection runs only on page reload

questions.explanation: Reachability, not the original local scope ending, determines whether an object can be collected.

questions.label: Respect worker boundaries
questions.prompt: Which operation belongs on the browser main thread rather than directly in a dedicated worker?
questions.explanation: Dedicated workers have no direct access to the document DOM.

questions.label: Use evidence to investigate responsiveness
questions.prompt: A main-thread trace shows a 300 ms JavaScript task during interaction. Which next step addresses that evidence?

choices.text: Assume a faster network will remove the task
Inspect its call stack and split, reduce or move appropriate computation
Add more synchronous work to the same task

questions.explanation: The trace points to main-thread computation; identify the work before choosing a mitigation.

questions.label: Order synchronous code and promise reactions
questions.prompt: A function logs `start`, schedules a resolved promise callback, then logs `end`. Can that callback run between those two synchronous logs?

choices.text: No, the current job completes first
Only if the promise resolves to a number

questions.explanation: Promise reactions do not interrupt the running JavaScript job.

questions.label: Track a captured binding
questions.prompt: Two functions close over the same mutable local variable. If one updates it, what can the other observe?

choices.text: Only its value at function creation

questions.explanation: Closures can share access to the same lexical binding.

courses.scope_note: A short sample of reasoning and prerequisite knowledge. Practical performance and durable mastery need later practice.

questions.label: Reason about structural compatibility
questions.prompt: `const source = { id: 1, label: "x" };` Can source be assigned to a variable of type `{ id: number }`?

choices.text: Yes, it has the required compatible member
No, every property must match exactly

questions.explanation: Structural assignability checks required members; fresh object literal excess-property checks are a separate rule.

questions.label: Separate types from runtime checks
questions.prompt: An HTTP response is asserted `as User`. What validation does that assertion perform at runtime?

choices.text: It throws when a field is missing

questions.explanation: A type assertion does not generate runtime validation code.

questions.label: Narrow before using a value
questions.prompt: For `value: string | number`, which condition permits `value.toUpperCase()` in its true branch?
questions.explanation: The typeof guard narrows this union to string.

questions.label: Preserve a relationship in an API
questions.prompt: Which signature preserves the input type as the output type for an identity function?

choices.text: function identity(value: string | number): string | number

questions.explanation: The type parameter ties the return type to the particular argument type.

questions.label: Validate external data
questions.prompt: A service receives untrusted JSON. Which boundary establishes that required fields have valid runtime values?

choices.text: Cast JSON.parse directly to the interface
Import the interface into the service
Parse and validate the unknown data before using a typed value

questions.explanation: Runtime checks establish data validity; interfaces alone are erased.

questions.label: Understand branded values
questions.prompt: A string brand distinguishes UserId and OrderId in TypeScript. What else is needed when reading an ID from a request?

choices.text: Runtime validation or a trusted constructor for the incoming value
Nothing; the brand encrypts the value

questions.explanation: A compile-time brand does not validate or authenticate external strings.

questions.label: Reason about structural compatibility
questions.prompt: A value stored in a variable has `{ x: 1, y: 2 }`. Is it structurally compatible with `{ x: number }`?

choices.text: No, extra members always forbid assignment

questions.explanation: The required x member is compatible; the question is not a fresh object literal excess-property check.

questions.label: Separate types from runtime checks
questions.prompt: Does changing `payload as string` convert a numeric payload into a string?

choices.text: No, assertions do not convert runtime values

questions.explanation: Use an explicit conversion or validation for runtime behavior.

questions.label: Choose a state owner
questions.prompt: A filter should survive reload and be shareable in a link. Where should its selected value usually be represented?

choices.text: Only in a global variable reset on reload

questions.explanation: The URL is an appropriate durable, shareable owner for navigational state.

questions.label: Keep one owner for controlled state
questions.prompt: A parent supplies a controlled input value. What should a reusable child normally do on edit?

choices.text: Keep an independent authoritative value forever
Write the parent variable through a global lookup
Emit the proposed change and render the supplied value

questions.explanation: A controlled contract keeps ownership explicit and avoids competing sources of truth.

questions.label: Preserve browser navigation meaning
questions.prompt: A user changes a search query and expects Back to restore the previous query. Which mechanism represents that navigation?

choices.text: A new history entry with the query in the URL

questions.explanation: A history entry allows the browser to restore the previous navigation state.

questions.label: Avoid cache identity collisions
questions.prompt: An app fetches project 7 for different signed-in tenants. What must a shared cache key distinguish?

choices.text: The relevant tenant or authorization context as well as project identity

questions.explanation: If the resource meaning varies by tenant, the cache identity must include that boundary.

questions.label: Plan mutation reconciliation
questions.prompt: After a successful edit, another screen shows a cached copy of the resource. What should the architecture define?

choices.text: That every cache stays unchanged indefinitely
That unrelated resource keys are all renamed
How affected cached views update or invalidate

questions.explanation: Mutation and cache reconciliation must agree on resource identity and affected views.

questions.label: Connect rollout to observable outcomes
questions.prompt: A feature is enabled for 5% of users. Which evidence supports expanding the rollout?

choices.text: The absence of any user comments in the first minute
Relevant errors and product outcomes compared with the control under a defined decision rule
The number of files in the pull request

questions.explanation: A staged rollout needs observable criteria and a way to stop or reverse expansion.

questions.label: Choose a state owner
questions.prompt: Which state should a copied search-results URL normally include?
questions.explanation: Serializable navigation state makes the copied link meaningful.

questions.label: Keep one owner for controlled state
questions.prompt: A controlled toggle receives `checked=false` after requesting true. What value should it display?
questions.explanation: The supplied controlled value remains authoritative.

questions.label: Keep machine output usable
questions.prompt: A CLI writes JSON for another process. Where should an explanatory warning normally go?
questions.explanation: Separate diagnostics from the machine-readable stdout contract.

questions.label: Choose a syntax-aware transform
questions.prompt: A codemod renames a local variable while preserving unrelated strings and comments. Which representation supports that task?

choices.text: A global text replacement of every matching substring
A parsed syntax tree with binding information

questions.explanation: Syntax and binding context distinguish references from unrelated text.

questions.label: Invalidate dependent work
questions.prompt: Module A imports B, and B changes. What must a correct incremental build consider?

choices.text: Only the last file opened in the editor
B and affected dependents of B
Only files whose names start with B

questions.explanation: The dependency graph identifies outputs that may depend on changed input.

questions.label: Identify shared-state leakage
questions.prompt: A test passes alone but fails after another test mutates a module-level cache. What is the likely missing boundary?

choices.text: State isolation or explicit cache reset between tests

questions.explanation: Order dependence points to shared mutable state crossing test boundaries.

questions.label: Check repeat-run safety
questions.prompt: A migration codemod may be rerun after interruption. Which property is useful?

choices.text: Every run adds the same import again
The tool ignores parse failures and rewrites all files
Already-transformed code is recognized and not transformed again

questions.explanation: Recognizing the target state supports safe repeat runs and recovery.

questions.label: Track inputs for reproducibility
questions.prompt: A build reads an undeclared environment variable that changes its output. What should a reusable build cache do?

choices.text: Key only by the output filename
Include that relevant input in its identity or remove the dependency
Reuse the cached output regardless of the variable

questions.explanation: A cache can be correct only if its key accounts for inputs that influence the result.

questions.label: Keep machine output usable
questions.prompt: A command cannot open its required input file. Which CLI behavior communicates failure to a caller?

choices.text: Exit status zero with no output
A diagnostic on stderr and a nonzero exit status
A success message followed by malformed JSON

questions.explanation: A process caller needs a failure status; diagnostic text explains the cause.

questions.label: Choose a syntax-aware transform
questions.prompt: Why can blindly replacing `name` also damage `username` and string literals?

choices.text: The operating system changes identifiers randomly
Text replacement does not understand tokens or binding scope

questions.explanation: A syntax-aware transform can target the intended identifiers.

questions.label: Estimate a workload
questions.prompt: A service receives 120 requests per second steadily for one minute. About how many requests arrive?
questions.explanation: Multiply the rate by the 60-second interval.

questions.label: Reason about a lost response
questions.prompt: A payment succeeds but the response is lost. Which retry design helps avoid charging again for the same operation?

choices.text: Generate a new operation identity on each retry
Assume every timeout means no payment occurred
Reuse an operation key and return its recorded outcome

questions.explanation: A stable operation identity lets the service recognize a repeated request; the key and outcome must be recorded consistently.

questions.label: Check quorum overlap
questions.prompt: A replicated register has 3 replicas. A write reaches 2 and a read consults 2. What does their set size guarantee?

choices.text: The system automatically provides linearizability without further rules
The read and write sets overlap in at least one replica

questions.explanation: Set overlap follows from R + W > N; version and protocol rules are still needed to reason about the returned value.

questions.label: Recognize skew
questions.prompt: A tenant-based shard key places 60% of traffic from one tenant on one shard. What is the immediate issue?

choices.text: A hot partition despite more total shards

questions.explanation: A heavily used key can concentrate work even when the cluster has spare capacity elsewhere.

questions.label: Coordinate state with event publication
questions.prompt: An order and its outgoing event must survive a process crash together. Which boundary is the transactional outbox designed around?

choices.text: Commit the order and hope a later in-memory callback always runs
Publish first and ignore database failure
Commit the order and outbox record in one database transaction, then publish from the outbox

questions.explanation: The transaction retains a durable publication intention alongside the state change; delivery still requires retry and consumer deduplication.

questions.label: Protect a dependency under failure
questions.prompt: A recommendation dependency times out during checkout. Which defined behavior can preserve the essential flow?

choices.text: Block all checkout requests until recommendations recover
Use a bounded timeout and an acceptable checkout fallback
Retry forever inside the user request

questions.explanation: A bounded dependency budget and a product-approved fallback can preserve the essential operation.

questions.label: Estimate a workload
questions.prompt: At a steady 25 requests per second for 4 seconds, how many requests arrive?
questions.explanation: Multiply requests per second by seconds.

questions.label: Reason about a lost response
questions.prompt: A client retries the same operation after a timeout. What must be stable to recognize it as the same request?

choices.text: A new random identity for every attempt
The operation identity used for deduplication
The TCP connection for the lifetime of the account

questions.explanation: Stable operation identity permits consistent retry handling across connections.

courses.scope_note: A short sample of reading, grammar and meaning. This is a provisional study suggestion, not a CEFR certification.

questions.label: A1: identify a meeting time
questions.prompt: Read: „Der Kurs beginnt am Montag um neun Uhr.“ Wann beginnt der Kurs?
questions.explanation: The sentence gives Montag and neun Uhr.

questions.label: A1: match a verb to its subject
questions.prompt: Choose the form: „Ich ___ in Berlin.“
questions.explanation: With ich, wohnen takes the form wohne.

questions.label: A2: interpret a changed arrangement
questions.prompt: Read: „Der Termin am Dienstag fällt aus. Wir treffen uns stattdessen am Donnerstag.“ Was gilt jetzt?

choices.text: Es gibt nie wieder ein Treffen

questions.explanation: Stattdessen introduces Thursday as the replacement.

questions.label: A2: place a verb in a reason clause
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with standard word order.

choices.text: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil bin ich krank.
Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich bin krank.

questions.explanation: In this weil subordinate clause, the finite verb bin comes at the end.

questions.label: B1: distinguish intention from a condition
questions.prompt: Read: „Ich würde gern am Kurs teilnehmen. Allerdings kann ich erst zusagen, wenn mein Dienstplan feststeht.“ Hat die Person schon fest zugesagt?

choices.text: Nein, sie möchte auf keinen Fall teilnehmen
Nein, die Zusage hängt noch vom Dienstplan ab

questions.explanation: The person expresses interest but makes confirmation dependent on the schedule.

questions.label: B1: understand an unreal condition
questions.prompt: „Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich öfter lesen.“ Was wird ausgedrückt?

choices.text: Ein Befehl an eine andere Person
Ein vorgestellter Zustand und seine mögliche Folge

questions.explanation: Hätte and würde express a hypothetical condition and consequence here.

questions.label: A1: identify a meeting time
questions.prompt: Read: „Die Bibliothek schließt heute um sechs Uhr.“ Was passiert um sechs Uhr?
questions.explanation: Schließt means closes in this sentence.

questions.label: A1: match a verb to its subject
questions.prompt: Choose the form: „Ich ___ Deutsch.“
questions.explanation: With ich, lernen takes the form lerne.

courses.scope_note: A short sample of reading, grammar and meaning. This is a provisional study suggestion, not a CEFR certification.

questions.label: A1: identify a meeting time
questions.prompt: Leggi: «Il corso inizia lunedì alle nove.» Quando inizia?
questions.explanation: The sentence gives lunedì and alle nove.

questions.label: A1: match a verb to its subject
questions.prompt: Scegli la forma: «Io ___ a Roma.»
questions.explanation: With io, abitare takes the form abito.

questions.label: A2: interpret a changed arrangement
questions.prompt: Leggi: «L’incontro di martedì è annullato. Ci vediamo invece giovedì.» Qual è il nuovo giorno?
questions.explanation: Invece introduces Thursday as the replacement.

questions.label: A2: understand completed action
questions.prompt: «Ieri ho comprato un libro.» Quando è avvenuto l’acquisto?
questions.explanation: Ieri and ho comprato refer to a completed past action.

questions.label: B1: distinguish intention from a condition
questions.prompt: Leggi: «Vorrei partecipare al corso, ma potrò confermare solo quando conoscerò i miei turni di lavoro.» La partecipazione è già confermata?

choices.text: No, la conferma dipende ancora dai turni

questions.explanation: The speaker wants to attend but cannot confirm before knowing the work shifts.

questions.label: B1: understand an unreal condition
questions.prompt: «Se avessi più tempo, leggerei di più.» Che cosa esprime la frase?

choices.text: Una condizione ipotetica e la sua conseguenza

questions.explanation: The sentence presents a hypothetical condition with a conditional consequence.

questions.label: A1: identify a meeting time
questions.prompt: Leggi: «La biblioteca chiude oggi alle sei.» Che cosa succede alle sei?
questions.explanation: Chiude means closes in this sentence.

questions.label: A1: match a verb to its subject
questions.prompt: Scegli la forma: «Io ___ italiano.»
questions.explanation: With io, studiare takes the form studio.
